rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s secretary of state sees uptick in business fraud with 3,508 complaints in two years
rows.standfirst: Investigations are ongoing and the office can now slap a “fraudulent” label on the baddies. Plus: Colorado down to 1.1 jobs per job seeker, union activity on the rise, lots of charts and more!

rows.title: How the Colorado Labor Peace Act came to be and why unions want so desperately to get rid of it
rows.standfirst: Democrats in the Colorado legislature this year want to get rid of the requirement that unions take a vote before they can negotiate with an employer over imposing fees on all employees to pay for collective bargaining

rows.title: Can employers in Colorado require a doctor’s note any time an employee calls in sick?
rows.standfirst: No. Under Colorado law, employers can ask for “reasonable documentation” only after absences of four or more consecutive days

rows.title: King Soopers workers to go on 14-day strike starting Thursday
rows.standfirst: After union members approved a strike, UFCW Local 7 said a two-week walkout will “allow everyone to understand our concerns.”

rows.title: Colorado public media outlets express concern at Trump’s FCC investigation threat
rows.standfirst: “This isn’t being done in isolation,” First Amendment attorney Steve Zansberg said. “There’s much more of this to come.”

rows.title: Colorado is on track to raise the minimum age to buy firearm ammunition to 21
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1133 is promoted as a way to align the rules for ammunition sales in Colorado with the new law prohibiting anyone younger than 21 from purchasing a gun

rows.title: Colorado’s high egg prices are blamed on bird flu, but there’s more to the story
rows.standfirst: Egg-laying chicken farmers are still recovering from the virus outbreak of 2022 but now there’s the new cage-free law, mutations and more competition as bird flu devastates other states.

rows.title: In Colorado’s war against NIMBYism, Democrats want to give churches the right to build housing
rows.standfirst: This week, Colorado Democrats introduced legislation to become one of the first states in the country to allow religious institutions to build housing on their land — whether it’s zoned for residential construction or not

rows.title: Mistrust bubbles up as nuclear waste storage talks come to rural Colorado
rows.standfirst: A nuclear waste watchdog group in Cañon City wants other communities that are considering partnering with the government on future waste storage plans to have the full picture of the energy cycle and its history.

rows.title: King Soopers hired temp workers to keep stores open during strike; pharmacies will close Sundays
rows.standfirst: The two-week labor stoppage has begun in Denver-area stores. Pueblo stores start will join on Friday. See the list of impacted stores and pharmacies.

rows.title: What’s Working: Public support for unions is high. But a Colorado grocery store strike on Super Bowl weekend?
rows.standfirst: King Soopers workers enter their first weekend on strike in the Pueblo and Denver areas. Plus: Grocery workers wages, lots of labor news and more!

rows.title: Trump orders US to stop production of pennies, billions of which are made in Denver
rows.standfirst: Pennies made in Denver and Philadelphia account for more than half the coins minted in 2024, but are they worth the effort?

rows.title: The King Soopers strike could cost Colorado Girl Scouts hundreds of thousands of dollars in cookie sales
rows.standfirst: Girl Scouts of Colorado CEO Leanna Clark said the girls in green and tan sold 3.7 million packages of cookies in 2024, many outside King Soopers stores

rows.title: Trump picks oil and gas advocate from Colorado to lead Bureau of Land Management
rows.standfirst: Kathleen Sgamma leads the Denver-based oil and gas trade group Western Energy Alliance

rows.title: Denver, Boulder restaurants could pay tipped workers less when their gratuities exceed minimum wage under proposed law
rows.standfirst: Restaurant owners say that changing the tip credit will go further to ease inflationary costs and help them survive. About 21,000 tipped workers in Colorado could see a dip in base pay, but tips or their employer would make it to minimum wage.

rows.title: Did Colorado have one of the highest marriage rates in the US in 2023?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Colorado’s marriage rates among men and women were in the top 5 nationwide, beating the national average.

rows.title: Bipartisan bill would let Colorado counties triple lodging taxes to pay for more than affordable housing
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1247 would allow voters to increase lodging taxes and use the revenue for infrastructure, law enforcement and conservation

rows.title: What’s Working: Higher egg, gas prices raise Denver inflation in January but rate still lower than the U.S.
rows.standfirst: Why is that? Economists share some obvious and not so obvious reasons. Plus: King Soopers gets temporary restraining order against striking workers as union downplays impact

rows.title: Can suspending a cage-free egg law solve the soaring price problem? Nevada takes a crack at it.
rows.standfirst: It is not clear dropping cage-free laws will have a significant effect on egg prices that have peaked at an average of $4.95 per dozen

rows.title: Would all guns with detachable magazines be banned in Colorado under Senate Bill 3?
rows.standfirst: No. Colorado Senate Bill 3 would ban sales of a broad swath — but not all — guns that use detachable magazines.

rows.title: Annual Colorado homeless count expected to show more people in shelters than usual because it was so cold
rows.standfirst: The annual Point in Time count included volunteers in 54 rural and mountain counties who counted people living outside and in shelters

rows.title: Interstate power lines threaten farmers’ land in southeastern Colorado
rows.standfirst: A federal plan to accelerate electrical grid updates is meeting major resistance in communities across the country, including three Colorado counties

rows.title: Colorado company can’t avoid $1.9M fine for oil and gas violations, even if it shuts down, court rules
rows.standfirst: Denver-based operator of low-producing wells argued state regulators imposed excessive fines related to violations, which now number 148 since 2020

rows.title: Outside expands its outdoors media empire with acquisition of booking software developer
rows.standfirst: Outside CEO Robin Thurston said his 450 employees are nearing 1 million subscribers as he focuses on profitability and hopefully going public in the next four years

rows.title: King Soopers and grocery workers end strike for 100 days as bargaining resumes
rows.standfirst: No tentative contract was reached yet, but the sides agreed to get back to the table to negotiate. Some workers were at risk of losing health coverage.

rows.title: Troubled Aurora apartment complex made infamous by Trump is now empty and boarded up
rows.standfirst: A nonprofit used $76,000 in grants and donations to help residents, many of them Venezuelan migrants, move into new housing

rows.title: How Colorado lawmakers and the governor want to incentivize the construction of affordable condos
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1272 would rewrite the so-called construction defect liability rules for condos sold for up to $1.2 million. The measure’s sponsors are hoping to find a sweet spot where everyone is a little unhappy.

rows.title: Effort to save restaurants by reducing base pay for tipped workers in Denver, Boulder clears first Colorado Capitol hurdle
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1208 would lower tipped-worker pay by as much as $4 an hour in Denver, but that reduction would go far in helping restaurants. During hours of committee testimony Thursday, lawmakers heard an array of differing opinions on the measure.

rows.title: What’s Working: Federal workers on Colorado unemployment benefits. Who pays?
rows.standfirst: Fired for “performance” doesn’t mean it’s your fault, says Colorado’s labor department. Plus: Ibotta cuts 8% of staff, Grand Junction mining jobs, another non-profit unionizes, more!

rows.title: The quest for water heads to the moon, via spacecraft built in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The Lockheed Martin space division in Littleton built the Lunar Trailblazer satellite, which will orbit the moon to locate where water may be hiding

rows.title: $3.2B in funding for Colorado rural electric co-ops and Tri-State frozen as clean energy programs are reconsidered
rows.standfirst: New ERA program grants to help close coal power plants and add renewable generation are stalled by review of “Marxist equity, transgenderism and green new deal social engineering policies”

rows.title: Some National Park and Forest service jobs restored. More seasonal hires promised.
rows.standfirst: In Colorado, a handful of firings appear to have been reversed, including the timber strike team, but Florissant Fossil Beds has pared hours

rows.title: Xcel faces challenges sending natural gas to Colorado mountain towns from its Boulder County station
rows.standfirst: Population growth combined with state-mandated energy benchmarks are straining the Marshall Compressor Station’s ability to meet gas demand in Summit and Grand counties, according to a company analysis

rows.title: Colorado Democrats split over payday borrowing services as consumer groups raise concerns
rows.standfirst: Industry officials insist “earned wage access” services aren’t a loan. If they were, they would violate a voter-approved state law limiting the interest rates payday lenders can charge.

rows.title: Xcel’s $155M plan to fix potential gas shortages in Colorado mountains will get a closer look by regulators
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s Public Utilities Commissioners want to make sure it’s the lowest-cost solution to Xcel Energy’s last-mile in the mountains problem

rows.title: Mass firings of probationary federal workers begin at NOAA, including many in Boulder
rows.standfirst: Employees received emails Thursday informing them of their abrupt termination, despite a U.S. District Court ruling calling the legality of such firing into question

rows.title: A Colorado bill to tap geothermal energy meets resistance from the hot springs industry
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1165 was created to iron out regulatory language about geothermal energy, but hot springs operators worry it will be too easy for developers to draw from their main resource
